_comment: Consumers that a nodus-lang release can invalidate but the Stage 6 downstream
sweep cannot see. That sweep works by hashing published sdists/wheels against
local source, so anything not on PyPI is invisible to it -- a VS Code extension
and a GitHub Action are both outside its reach, and both have shipped stale.
The check deliberately does NOT read the consumer's checkout. A gate that needs
a sibling clone skips on CI, and a check that skips where it matters is how a
keyword shipped unhighlighted in the first place. Instead each consumer records
the fingerprint of whatever it must stay in step with, measured HERE, at the
moment it was last published. When the live value moves, the consumer is stale.
To add one: name what it tracks, run the gate, and paste the value it reports.
To clear a stale flag: republish the consumer, then update `fingerprint` and

consumers.name: nodus-vscode
consumers.why: The TextMate grammar lists every keyword explicitly. A keyword the grammar does not name renders as a plain identifier, so any keyword added or removed here makes the published extension wrong.
consumers.republish: Bump version in package.json, `npm run package`, then upload the VSIX at https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/manage/publishers/MasterplanInfiniteWeave (row menu -> Update), or `npx vsce publish -p <PAT>`.

consumers.name: nodus-run-action
consumers.why: Its README documents a pinned `version:` for reproducible CI. The pin is the version new users copy, so it going stale hands them an old runtime.
consumers.republish: Update the pinned `version:` in README.md examples, then tag the action.
